title: The New International Encyclopaedia
corrections_note: 491,713 by the cleanup engine + 604 by the sentence context pass + 18 by the headword pass + 406 by the proofread pass.
source: HathiTrust record 001461834; Internet Archive first-edition scans (Dodd, Mead and Company, New York). Editors: Daniel Coit Gilman, Harry Thurston Peck, Frank Moore Colby. Vols. 1-5 dated 1902, vols. 6-14 dated 1903, vols. 15-17 dated 1904; all 17 title pages read as images. Second scans used as a check only, never merged.
pages_note: Article page numbers are the exact printed folios where the leafmap could anchor them. Vols. 13 and 15 each carry one unnumbered illustration plate that shifts the folio model by one (recorded as a break). Vol. 14 folios 59-62 are missing from the scan (a real gap, image-confirmed); that text is absent.
key_note: Keys are lowercase with non-alphanumerics stripped, as in the Britannica/Chambers's/Catholic builds. Leading digits are stripped from the KEY only (fused folio numbers); no headword in this data needed it, and the display headword is kept verbatim.
honest_limits: Article count is a lower bound: some headwords remain OCR-garbled and were not split into entries (ABMTELT, TYPEWRITEBS, BICE-BIBD, MELTINS POT, ARME'RIA for ARMENIA); the headword pass was deliberately conservative after a broader attempt falsely 'corrected' real proper names (reverted). The AFRICA article has no headword: its text survives only in fragments — the 'ISOO' tail at vol. 1, p. 184 is about West African boundaries. GERMANY is filed as GERMAN EMPIRE (vol. 8, p. 276) — the book's own heading, not a loss. Vol. 14 folios 59-62 are missing from the scan. Only vols. 1 and 9 have a first-edition second scan; the other 15 volumes rest on a single scan. Vol. 13's candidate second scan was rejected (it is the 1928 second edition, not the first). Front matter (title page, illustrations list, pronunciation key, preface) was not run through the cleanup engine. No full word-by-word proofread — the proofread pass covered the most frequent unresolved tokens only. 219,190 distinct unresolved tokens remain (356,637 occurrences, 2.07% of words), mostly real proper names, foreign words and Latin.
